title: A point of a limit is the limit of its images
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ and projections $f_i:S\to S_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $s\in S$ and $s_i=f_i(s)$. Then the field maps $\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(s_{i'})$ ($i'\ge i$) and $\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(s)$ induced by $f_{i'i}$ and $f_i$ [def-weil-residue-field] make $\kappa(s)$ the directed colimit $\varinjlim_i\kappa(s_i)$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; equivalently $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$, is the limit of the inverse system $(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i))_i$ (whose transition morphisms are affine) in the category of schemes, compatibly with the canonical morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)\to S_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$.

source.place: Limits, Lemma Tag 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), part (1), and its proof (reduction to S_i affine, then A/p = colim A_i/p_i)

proof.text: *Step 1 (the system of residue fields and the cocone).* A directed set is nonempty (Stacks, Categories, Definition 00D3), so $I\neq\emptyset$. For $i'\ge i$ the cone identity $f_{i'i}\circ f_{i'}=f_i$ gives $f_{i'i}(s_{i'})=s_i$, so $f_{i'i}$ induces a field map $r_{i'i}:\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(s_{i'})$ and $f_i$ induces $\rho_i:\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The residue map of a composite of morphisms is the composite of the residue maps and that of an identity is the identity (the residue maps are induced by the stalk maps, which compose), so $r_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $r_{i''i'}\circ r_{i'i}=r_{i''i}$ for $i''\ge i'\ge i$, and $\rho_{i'}\circ r_{i'i}=\rho_i$ (from $f_{i'i}\circ f_{i'}=f_i$). Thus $i\mapsto\kappa(s_i)$ is a diagram of commutative rings over the directed set $I$ (viewed as a filtered category) and $(\kappa(s),(\rho_i))$ is a cocone on it [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The claim is that this cocone is a colimit.

source.place: Lemma 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), proof, first paragraph (reduction to the affine case)

proof.text: *Step 2 (reduction to $I_{\ge0}$).* Choose $0\in I$. Every $i\in I$ has some $j\in I_{\ge0}$ with $j\ge i$ ($I$ directed). By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1), applied with $\mathcal C$ = commutative rings, $\mathcal I$ the cofiltered category of $I$ ($\operatorname{Hom}(j,i)=\{*\}$ iff $j\ge i$), $\mathcal J=I_{\ge0}$ and $D:i\mapsto\kappa(s_i)$: if the restricted diagram $(\kappa(s_i))_{i\ge0}$ has a colimit then so has $D$, and the canonical map $c:\varinjlim_{i\ge0}\kappa(s_i)\to\varinjlim_{i\in I}\kappa(s_i)$ is an isomorphism. Suppose $(\kappa(s),(\rho_i)_{i\ge0})$ is a colimit of the restricted diagram. The cocone $(\kappa(s),(\rho_i)_{i\in I})$ of step 1 induces $u:\varinjlim_I\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(s)$ with $u\circ\iota_i=\rho_i$; then $u\circ c$ is the map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s)$ compatible with the $\rho_i$, $i\ge0$, i.e. the identity, so $u=c^{-1}$ is an isomorphism and $(\kappa(s),(\rho_i)_{i\in I})$ is a colimit of $D$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. So it suffices to prove that $(\kappa(s),(\rho_i)_{i\ge0})$ is a colimit of $(\kappa(s_i))_{i\ge0}$.

source.place: Lemma 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), proof, first paragraph (reduction to the affine case)

proof.text: *Step 3 (reduction to an affine neighbourhood).* Choose an affine open $U_0\subseteq S_0$ containing $s_0$ (every point of a scheme has an affine open neighbourhood [def-pc-scheme]); put $U_i=f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)\subseteq S_i$ ($i\ge0$) and $U=f_0^{-1}(U_0)\subseteq S$, open subschemes. Then $s\in U$ and $s_i\in U_i$, as $f_{i0}(s_i)=f_0(s)=s_0\in U_0$. Each $U_i$ is affine, being the preimage of the affine open $U_0$ under the affine morphism $f_{i0}$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism] ($f_{00}=\mathrm{id}$). By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] (the clause on an open $U_0$ of $S_0$), $(U_i)_{i\ge0}$ with the restricted transition morphisms is an inverse system with affine transition morphisms over the directed set $I_{\ge0}$, and $U$ with the restricted projections $f_i|_U:U\to U_i$ is its limit. Let $u:U\to S$, $u_i:U_i\to S_i$ be the open immersions; then $f_i\circ u=u_i\circ f_i|_U$ and $f_{i'i}\circ u_{i'}=u_i\circ f_{i'i}|_{U_{i'}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] the residue maps $\kappa_S(s)\to\kappa_U(s)$ and $\kappa_{S_i}(s_i)\to\kappa_{U_i}(s_i)$ induced by $u$, $u_i$ are isomorphisms, and by functoriality of residue maps (step 1) the two commutative squares turn them into an isomorphism from the diagram $(\kappa_{S_i}(s_i))_{i\ge0}$ with cocone $(\kappa_S(s),(\rho_i))$ onto the diagram $(\kappa_{U_i}(s_i))_{i\ge0}$ with the cocone of residue maps of the $f_i|_U$. A cocone isomorphic to a colimit cocone is a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Hence it suffices to prove the statement for the system $(U_i)_{i\ge0}$, its limit $U$ and the point $s\in U$: i.e. we may assume that $0$ is the least element of $I$ and that $S_0$ and hence all $S_i$ are affine.

source.place: Lemma 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), proof, first paragraph (reduction to the affine case)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the affine case: translation to rings).* Assume all $S_i$ affine. Put $A_i=\Gamma(S_i,\mathcal O_{S_i})$, with $\varphi_{ii'}=f_{ii'}^\sharp:A_{i'}\to A_i$ for $i\ge i'$, and $A=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ with $\iota_i=f_i^\sharp:A_i\to A$; so $\iota_i\circ\varphi_{ii'}=\iota_{i'}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] (affine case) $S\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_iA_i)$ is affine. An affine scheme $X$ is canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and morphisms between them are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of their maps on global sections [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; so after these identifications $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $f_{ii'}=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi_{ii'}$, $f_i=\operatorname{Spec}\iota_i$ (isomorphisms of schemes compatible with all morphisms induce, by functoriality of residue maps, an isomorphism of the diagrams of residue fields and of the cocones, as in step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-global-sections-colimit] (the $S_i$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated) $(A,(\iota_i))$ is a colimit of $(A_i,\varphi_{ii'})$ in commutative rings. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be the prime ideal $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-residue-field-naturality](1), $s_i=\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_i)(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p_i:=\iota_i^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$, and $\varphi_{ii'}^{-1}(\mathfrak p_i)=\mathfrak p_{i'}$. By part (2) of the same node, the isomorphisms $e_A:\kappa_S(s)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ and $e_{A_i}:\kappa_{S_i}(s_i)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ carry $\rho_i$ to $\kappa(\iota_i):\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $r_{ii'}$ to $\kappa(\varphi_{ii'})$ (the maps $x/t\mapsto\iota_i(x)/\iota_i(t)$, resp. $\varphi_{ii'}(x)/\varphi_{ii'}(t)$, modulo the maximal ideals). By step 3's remark on isomorphic cocones it remains to show: $(\kappa(\mathfrak p),(\kappa(\iota_i)))$ is a colimit of $(\kappa(\mathfrak p_i),\kappa(\varphi_{ii'}))$ in commutative rings (steps 5-6).

source.place: Lemma 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), proof, second paragraph (A = colim A_i, p_i = phi_i^{-1}(p), kappa(p) = colim kappa(p_i))

proof.text: *Step 5 (algebra: every element of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ comes from a stage, and the maps are injective).* Put $\bar\iota_i=\kappa(\iota_i)$, $\bar\varphi_{ii'}=\kappa(\varphi_{ii'})$. (a) Cocone: for $i\ge i'$, $\bar\iota_i\circ\bar\varphi_{ii'}$ sends the class of $x/t$ to the class of $\iota_i\varphi_{ii'}(x)/\iota_i\varphi_{ii'}(t)=\iota_{i'}(x)/\iota_{i'}(t)$, so $\bar\iota_i\circ\bar\varphi_{ii'}=\bar\iota_{i'}$; similarly $\bar\varphi$ is functorial. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime](2) (the directed set $I$ is a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), $A_{\mathfrak p}$ with the maps $\kappa_i:(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}\to A_{\mathfrak p}$, $x/t\mapsto\iota_i(x)/\iota_i(t)$, is a colimit of $i\mapsto(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ in commutative rings; commutative rings being commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebras, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](2) shows that every element of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\kappa_i(w)$ for some $i$ and $w\in(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is surjective and the class of $\kappa_i(w)$ is $\bar\iota_i$ of the class of $w$, every element of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is $\bar\iota_i(a)$ for some $i$ and $a\in\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$. (c) Each $\bar\iota_i$ is a ring homomorphism between fields, hence injective (its kernel is an ideal of the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ not containing $1$).

source.place: Lemma 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), proof, second paragraph (A = colim A_i, p_i = phi_i^{-1}(p), kappa(p) = colim kappa(p_i))

proof.text: *Step 6 (algebra: universal property).* Let $(T,(g_i:\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)\to T))$ be a cocone of commutative rings on $(\kappa(\mathfrak p_i),\bar\varphi_{ii'})$. For $z\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ write $z=\bar\iota_i(a)$ (step 5(b)) and set $g(z)=g_i(a)$. Well defined: if $\bar\iota_i(a)=\bar\iota_j(b)$, choose $k\ge i,j$ ($I$ directed) and put $a'=\bar\varphi_{ki}(a)$, $b'=\bar\varphi_{kj}(b)$; by step 5(a) $\bar\iota_k(a')=\bar\iota_k(b')$, so $a'=b'$ by step 5(c), and $g_i(a)=g_k(a')=g_k(b')=g_j(b)$. Ring map: two elements $z,z'$ are, after moving to a common $k\ge i,j$ as above, $\bar\iota_k(a),\bar\iota_k(a')$, so $g(z+z')=g_k(a+a')=g(z)+g(z')$, $g(zz')=g(z)g(z')$, and $g(1)=g_i(1)=1$. By construction $g\circ\bar\iota_i=g_i$; any $h$ with $h\circ\bar\iota_i=g_i$ for all $i$ equals $g$ because the images of the $\bar\iota_i$ cover $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (step 5(b)). Hence $(\kappa(\mathfrak p),(\bar\iota_i))$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], which with steps 2-4 proves $\kappa(s)=\varinjlim_i\kappa(s_i)$ via the maps $\rho_i$, for the original system over $I$.

source.place: Lemma 0CUG (lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles, line 332), proof, second paragraph (A = colim A_i, p_i = phi_i^{-1}(p), kappa(p) = colim kappa(p_i))

proof.text: *Step 7 (the scheme-theoretic form).* By steps 1-6, $(\kappa(s),(\rho_i))$ is the colimit of the directed system of commutative rings $(\kappa(s_i),r_{i'i})$ over $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}(\rho_i):\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)$ is the limit in the category of schemes of the inverse system $(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i),\operatorname{Spec}(r_{i'i}))$, whose transition morphisms are affine (morphisms between affine schemes) [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Compatibility: let $j_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ and $j_{s_i}:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i)\to S_i$ be the canonical morphisms; [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to $f_i$ at $s$ and to $f_{i'i}$ at $s_{i'}$ gives $f_i\circ j_s=j_{s_i}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\rho_i)$ and $f_{i'i}\circ j_{s_{i'}}=j_{s_i}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r_{i'i})$, i.e. the morphisms $j_{s_i}$ form a morphism of inverse systems $(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_i))\to(S_i)$ whose limit is $j_s$.
